title: Determination 45/1/210: two site-manufactured plywood web beams in a roof-space conversion
jurisdiction: England (UK): Secretary of State determination / appeal / tribunal under the Building Act 1984 and Building Regulations; comparative test only, not Alberta
code_edition: Building Regulations 2000 (as amended): Regulation 7 and Requirement A1 (as cited)

facts.text: Proposed work: a roof-space conversion at a new second-floor level of a four-bedroom, two-storey semi-detached house; the ceiling is supported on plywood web beams.
The applicant's proposals assume the plywood web beams will be manufactured at site.

The Borough Council rejected the full plans application for non-compliance with regulation 14 (provision of details) and other items; its main concern was the stability of the two beams and their site manufacture.
The applicant's calculations follow BS 5268: Part 2: 1984 and TRADA guidance and argue that site manufacture can achieve high precision.
The Council cited BS 6446: 1997 for glued-component manufacture and quality control, and quoted BRE IP 7/88 that workmanship is the most important factor in beam performance.
The Secretary of State regards the glueline between flange and ply web as critical and is 'very concerned' about site manufacture; drawing MAC/NM/07 shows finger joints in the flanges.
Determination: the proposals, incorporating design and manufacture at site of two plywood web beams, do not comply with Regulation 7 (materials and workmanship) or Requirement A1 (loading).
